title: A nonconstant morphism of curves with normal target is flat
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be curves over $k$: separated integral schemes of finite type and dimension one [def-pc-curve]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism whose image contains at least two points. Suppose $Y$ is normal, meaning that every local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Then $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism].

proof.text: By [def-pc-curve], $X$ is integral and $Y$ is a curve. Apply [lem-a1-nonconstant-curve-stalk-torsion-free] to $f$, using the given two-point image. It gives dominance and, for every $x\in X$, an injective map $A=\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}\to B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for which $B$ is a torsion-free $A$-module.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, proof: nonconstant, dominant, injective stalk maps, torsion-free modules

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-normal-curve-local-principal-domains] to the normal curve $Y$. At $y=f(x)$ its local ring $A$ is Noetherian of dimension at most one and is either a field or a discrete valuation ring; in both cases it is a principal ideal domain. This applies also when $y$ is the generic point.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, proof: field-or-DVR target local rings

proof.text: Fix any $x\in X$. Step 1 gives a torsion-free $A$-module $B$ and Step 2 gives a principal ideal domain $A$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] makes $B$ flat over $A$, with no finite-generation assumption on $B$. Since this holds at every $x$, [def-weil-flat-morphism] says exactly that $f$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, proof: torsion-free implies flat (Tag 0539), then stalkwise flatness (Tag 01U3)

I mapped all seven old steps to their new places. lem-a1-nonconstant-curve-stalk-torsion-free takes the generic-point and topological-dimension part of old step 1, old steps 2 and 5, and the torsion part of old step 6. Its statement is true for any integral source: a non-generic image of η_X would be closed by the chain argument, giving a one-point image; the germ square with an injective field map then makes φ injective, and B is a domain, so B is torsion-free. lem-a1-normal-curve-local-principal-domains takes the local-dimension bound of old step 1 and old steps 3–4: stalks are Noetherian, a field in dimension 0, a DVR in dimension 1 (normal Noetherian), hence PIDs. No separability is needed. The two nodes are of comparable size (about 2.2k and 1.8k characters of old argument), independent of each other, and neither restates the item. The assembly is 3 steps of about 900 characters: the two nodes, then lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat (no finite generation needed) and def-weil-flat-morphism.
